chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa'at, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I buy the slave girl, and sometimes her menstruation is withheld due to spoilage of blood or wind in the womb, so she is given medicine for that, and she menstruates from that day. Is it permissible for me to do that, while I do not know if that is from pregnancy or from something else?' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do not do that'.

So I said to him: 'But rather, her menstruation had been withheld from her for a month, and if that were from pregnancy, it would have been a seed like the seed of the man who isolates (ejaculates outside).' So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The seed, when it falls into the womb, becomes a clot, then a chewed lump, then to whatever Allah wills; and when the seed falls into other than the womb, nothing is created from it. Therefore, do not give her the medicine when her menstruation is withheld for a month, and her usual time for menstruation has passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving medicine to induce menstruation when pregnancy is uncertain?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against inducing menstruation with medicine when pregnancy is uncertain, distinguishing between the womb, where the seed develops into an 'alaqah and mudghah, and other body parts where no formation occurs. This ruling specifically applies when menstruation is delayed for a month beyond her customary cycle, establishing a precautionary principle to avoid harming a potential fetus. The hadith highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on embryological development in determining legal rulings regarding purity and pregnancy.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘I bought the slave girl. So sometimes her menstruation (Haydh) gets withheld from the spoilage of the blood, or wind in the womb. So she drinks the medicine for that, and she menstruates from that day. Is that allowed for me and I do not know whether that is from a pregnancy or from something else?’ So heasws said to me: ‘Do not do that’.

So I said to himasws, ‘But rather, her menstruation (Haydh) had been raised from her for months, and had that been from a pregnancy, rather it would have been a seed like the seed of the man who isolates (ejaculates outside)’. So heasws said to me: ‘The seed, when it falls into the womb, comes to be a cloth, to comes to be a lump, and to whatever Allahazwj so Desires; and when the seed falls into other than the womb, nothing is Created from it, therefore do not give her the medicine to drink when her menstruation (Haydh) is raised for months, or it exceeds her time which she was menstruating in previously’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from Rifa’ah who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I may purchase a slave-girl. Her Hayd (menses) stops because of spoiled blood or some kind of air in her womb, and she uses medicine for cure and her Hayd (menses) begins on the same day. I do not know if it is because of pregnancy or for other reasons, is it (use of medicine) permissible? He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not (allow to) do so?

I then said that her Hayd (menses) has stopped for a month. Were it because of pregnancy, it would be a seed like the seed of man for which he may use contraceptives. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the seed falls inside the womb, it changes into a lump, then into flesh, then into what Allah wills. If the seed (semen) falls in places other than the womb nothing is created thereof. You must not give her medicine, when her Hayd (menses) stops, for a month and her time of Hayd (menses) passes?” (Fatwa best explains the above Hadith; it deals with several issues such as contraceptives, liability for abortion and the stages of fetuses.)
